The '''1990–91 Primeira Divisão''' was the [[Primeira Liga#All-time Primeira Liga table|57th edition]] of top flight of Portuguese football. It started on 19 August 1990 with a match between [[S.C. Farense|Farense]] and [[C.D. Nacional|Nacional]], and ended on 26 May 1991. The league was contested by 20 clubs with [[FC Porto|Porto]]  as the defending champions.

[[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] qualified for the [[1991–92 European Cup]] first round, Porto qualified for the [[1991–92 European Cup Winners' Cup]] first round, and [[Sporting Clube de Portugal|Sporting CP]], [[Boavista F.C.|Boavista]]  and [[S.C. Salgueiros|Salgueiros]] qualified for the [[1991–92 UEFA Cup]] first round; in opposite, [[F.C. Tirsense|Tirsense]], [[Vitória F.C.|Vitória de Setúbal]], [[C.F. Estrela da Amadora|Estrela da Amadora]], [[C.F. Os Belenenses|Belenenses]] and [[C.D. Nacional|Nacional]] were relegated to the [[Liga de Honra]]. [[Rui Águas (footballer)|Rui Águas]] was the top scorer with 25 goals.

==Promotion and relegation==

===Teams relegated to [[Liga de Honra]]===
*[[Portimonense S.C.|Portimonense]]
*[[C.D. Feirense|Feirense]]

Portimonense and Feirense were consigned to the Liga de Honra following their final classification in [[1989–90 Primeira Divisão|1989-90 season]].

===Teams promoted from Liga de Honra===
*[[S.C. Salgueiros|Salgueiros]]
*[[Gil Vicente F.C.|Gil Vicente]]
*[[S.C. Farense|Farense]]
*[[F.C. Famalicão|Famalicão]]

The other two teams were replaced by Salgueiros, Gil Vicente, Farense and Famalicão from the Liga de Honra, as the league increase from 18 to 20 teams.
